episodes.195881: An anomalously strong upper low from the west over AZ resulted in shower activity across western NM on October 18th resulting in some high wind gusts across parts of western and central NM. As the upper low remained nearly stationary over AZ heading into October 19th, it helped pull up abundant moisture from the Gulf of Mexico into eastern NM producing widespread strong to severe storms over portions of the eastern plains, mainly south of I-25. Bands of showers and thunderstorms first produced very heavy rainfall over a long twelve to eighteen hour period totaling 2 to 6 inches over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. Thankfully there were only reports of nuisance flooding in this area on October 19th. Storms developing along the highlands late on the afternoon and evening of the 19th organized into a line over eastern portions of Lincoln County and western portions of Chaves County. This line of storms shifted eastward over the Pecos River Valley during the evening of the 19th producing historically high rainfall. The as of this date all-time record daily maximum rainfall amount at Roswell of 5.78 inches was recorded, with numerous other mesonet and public weather stations recording 4 to 9 inches in Roswell. Fatal flash flooding resulted in Roswell with reports of flooding inundating homes forcing people to their attics and rooftops, and vehicles being stranded and washed away. The Chaves County Sheriff recorded a video of himself being stranded on his vehicle alongside two other individuals in flood waters after trying to respond to an incident. River flooding was observed along the Rio Felix and Pecos River in Chaves County. This river flooding washed out NM Highway 2 in Hagerman along the Rio Felix. The Pecos River reached 20.34 feet at the Lake Arthur gage, which was minor stage before receding. The Chaves County Emergency Manager reported that flooding did not recede until Monday morning on October 22nd in Roswell. Another round of severe storms with damaging wind gusts and large hail impacted northeast NM during the evening and early overnight hours of October 20th before the storm system exited the state.||Key Impacts: Flash flooding, hail, thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.195969: A strong cut off low pressure system near the four-corners region generated extreme rainfall over eastern New Mexico from the 19th through the 20th. On the 21st, this system started to become absorbed back into the general flow of the atmosphere. As this occurred, the cut off low became an open wave trough moving over West Texas early in the morning on the 21st. Significant elevated instability brought scattered thunderstorms to the area early on the 21st. One of these storms produced severe hail and damaging winds near Needmore (Bailey County).
episodes.195989: Overnight on the 20th going into the 21st, a line of storms moved into eastern Colorado from the south-southwest. Multiple reports of 50-55 MPH winds were recorded, as was one measurement of 60 MPH.
episodes.195990: In the mid-day of the 21st, a cold front swept through the region causing multiple clusters of storms to form. One storm was able to produce hail up to one inch.
episodes.196175: An upper level low pressure over northeast Colorado early Monday morning lifted eastward, with a surface reflected cold front that tracked across western Kansas though the day.   Showers and some thunderstorms were associated with the cold front during the morning, and by afternoon the atmosphere ahead of the front allowed thunderstorms to become more robust, with a few sub criteria hail reports. A particularly strong thunderstorm produced golf ball hailstorms in Barber county, KS in the early afternoon.  Subsequent to the hailstorm in Barber county, a severe thunderstorm watch was issued for parts of central a west central Kansas, however additional updrafts in the Dodge City forecast area struggled to become mature thunderstorms.
episodes.197214: Showers moving onshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.197411: A closed low pressure center set-up over the desert southwest. The seasonality of it created cold enough temperatures for heavy snow over the mountains, but the position of the low at this point of the year created a sufficient enough atmosphere for severe thunderstorms over the eastern plains.
episodes.197414: After a new record flood level occurred on the Mendenhall River due to a Glacial Dam Lake Outburst Flood in August 2024, Suicide Basin refilled with rain through the fall and a second release from the basin occurred with a crest on October 20th.

events.narrative: Heavy rains resulting in the devastating flash flooding in Roswell swelled the Pecos River on October 20th, reaching the Lake Arthur gauge near the southern Chaves County line. River levels surpassed minor flood level at 20 feet at 17:30 MST, peaking at 20.34 feet at 7:30pm MST before receding below minor flood stage at 11:45pm MST that night.
A line of strong storms dropped penny size hail across Santa Fe.
A strong storm dropped penny size hail with accumulations of 2 to 3 inches.

A facebook post from the Cunico Ranch in Colfax County showed severe thunderstorm wind damage, including the destruction a detached garage or shed, and the roof being torn off another building that had been constructed over 100 years ago. Numerous other damage was shown to outdoor equipment and materials, including their power supply. Little visible damage was received to the barn and home. Damage is an estimate.
A nearby severe thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust at Melrose Air Force Range.

The Mendenhall Lake Gauge rose above the moderate flood stage of 10 feet at 715pm AKST on Sunday October 20th, crested at 10.8 feet at 1130pm, and fell below moderate flood stage at 1am AKDT on the 21st. There were reports of trees and debris floating down the river and water into some yards on View Drive. Skaters Cabin Road was closed and impassable along with some damage to the USFS Mendenhall Campground.
Hailstones were fused together, some the size of a golf ball.
Surface observations from KLHX.
A severe storm dropped penny to quarter size hail east of Tucumcari stripping leaves off trees.
A severe storm dropped golf ball size hail along I-40 east of Tucumcari.
A strong to severe storm dropped nickel size hail a few miles southeast of Logan.
A severe storm dropped ping pong size hail in southwest Union County.
Personal Weather Station kcocheye2 recorded a 60 MPH gust.
